text:
ops-bot: ALERT: sustained uptick in NVIDIA Xid errors (13 / 79) across eu-west1-a (A10s) and us-east1-c (H100 pool). 60m window, 0.8% of requests. Auto-notify to #eng-runtime :rotating_light:
elaine: saw the alert, pulling batch traces now. any recent deploys to rerank-batch-svc? :eyes:
vik: nope, no deploys. but we did enable cross-region spillover routing last night for dedicated tenants (policy: spill->us-east if eu-west latency>120ms).
raj: confirmed, spillover started around 03:12 UTC. correlating timeline: spillover -> smaller batches hitting the A10 embedder -> Xid 13 spikes.
ken: here's a quick log sample from the A10 host that OOM'd one card then produced Xid 13s:
```
[2026-03-20T03:17:42Z] GPU0: Xid 13: CE error on channel 0000:3b:00.0
[2026-03-20T03:17:42Z] NVML: ECC: corrected_error_count spikes
[2026-03-20T03:17:43Z] process rerank-batch-svc pid=2241 killed by oom_killer
```
elaine: interesting that ECC corrected spike precedes Xid 13 by 1s. that suggests a transient ECC storm not full card death. might be thermal or power transient.
tess: A10s in that rack had higher P12 power draws (~5% over baseline) during the spill. Could be batching change -> longer sequences -> more sustained power.
vik: also saw Xid 79 on a subset of H100s in us-east1 later that morning, but pattern different: Xid 79 correlated with long-running single-stream decodes (seq len > 1024) on dedicated tenants.
raj: hypoth: two independent root causes: eu-west A10s get micro-bursts from spilled small-batch rerank jobs causing ECC corrected bursts -> Xid 13 transiently; us-east H100 Xid 79 from decode driver edge-case when KV-cache eviction + large seqs happen simultaneously.
sre-bot: NOTE: flagged hosts 10.4.12.8/9/10 for soft-drain, added to maintenance window at 03:40 UTC.
ken: plan suggestion: 1) temporarily disable cross-region spillover for rerank-batch-svc (reduce A10 pressure), 2) enable retry/backoff on small-batch clients to accumulate into slightly larger batches, 3) soft-drain the noisy A10 cards and run memtest + ECC stress.
elaine: I can scope a quick prompt eval to replicate: run rerank-batch with batchsize=1, seq=96, parallel inflight 16 -> that'll reproduce the small-burst pattern. anyone want to own the repro?
vik: I will run repro against a staging A10 rack (schedule in 30m) and attach NVSM logs.
raj: I'll collect nvml/error counters across eu-west racks for the 6h window and plot correlation with spillover events.
tess: ops: please confirm soft-drain doesn't violate Dedicated tenant SLAs; if it does, we'll need immediate replacement route for those tenants.
sre-bot: SLA check: Dedicated tenant "datasci-inc" on region eu-west1 has 99.9% availability target; soft-drain for 20m is within maintenance SLA if we route traffic to standby pool.
ken: Action items: vik repro (30m), raj gather nvml+routing logs (1h), elaine hold off on disabling spillover until we have repro but prepare rollback plan (10m). I'll file a short incident ticket and tag hardware team to run memory stress if soft-drain confirms hardware instability. :thumbsup:
elaine: one more note — if ECC corrected counts are persistently high, we should consider deprecating that specific A10 board (replacement + RMA). want to avoid latent failures.
vik: repro started. attaching quick trace here (pasted):
```
rerank client -> A10 host 10.4.12.9
batch=1 inflight=16 seq=96
NVML: ecc_corrected: 0 -> 48 in 12s
dmesg: Xid 13 on gpu 2
```
raj: plot ready, sending link in thread (internal link): https://grafana.internal/runs/3312345678/xid-corr (note: shows tight correlation with spillover rate).
tess: moving the rerank spillover throttle to 30rps for 45m reduces A10 error rate to baseline in the simulation.
sre-bot: REMINDER: if soft-drain completes and memtest passes, clear host from maintenance. record RMA if memtest fails.
ken: good triage. we'll keep monitoring for 3h after remediation, and then decide on replacement. closing loop in standup at 16:00 UTC. :calendar:
